metadata.summary: A dataset of 10,015 dermatoscopic images of pigmented skin lesions collected from two sources: a hospital-centered archive of the Department of Dermatology at the Medical University of Vienna, and a smaller public repository of the ISIC Archive. Annotated with 7 diagnostic categories for training and benchmarking machine learning models for automated skin lesion classification.
metadata.custodian: Medical University of Vienna; ISIC Archive
metadata.purpose: Training and benchmarking machine learning models for automated skin lesion classification.

papers.title: The HAM10000 dataset, a large collection of multi-source dermatoscopic images of common pigmented skin lesions

ethics.privacy_measures: Images de-identified; no patient identifiers retained.

extraction.notes: 基线卡仅来自 dataset_catalog.xlsx 真实元数据；其余字段需论文/README 或人工补充。

known_limitations: Predominantly Austrian population limits geographic generalizability.
Lack of reported demographic metadata (age, sex, ethnicity) hinders bias analysis.
Potential label noise due to variable diagnostic certainty (histopathology vs. clinical follow-up).
Uneven class distribution across 7 diagnostic categories.
bias_and_limitations.modifications: No synthetic data; minor preprocessing (rescaling, cropping) applied for standardization.
bias_sources: label bias (inter-observer variability, diagnostic modality heterogeneity)
bias_and_limitations.representativeness_concerns: Overrepresentation of Caucasian skin types and Austrian healthcare setting; limited representation of darker skin tones and low-resource settings.
bias_and_limitations.long_tail_classes: Yes — melanoma and seborrheic keratosis are most frequent; vascular lesions and basal cell carcinoma are rarer.
bias_and_limitations.generalizability_statement: Limited generalizability to non-Caucasian skin types, non-European clinical settings, and lesions outside the 7 diagnostic categories.
bias_and_limitations.missing_data: Demographic attributes (age, sex, ethnicity) are missing or unreported.

tasks_and_use.excluded_tasks: Detection and segmentation tasks are not supported by current annotation format (image-level labels only).

data_origin.selection_rationale: Images collected from clinical dermatology practice (Medical University of Vienna) and public dermoscopic repository (ISIC Archive) to create a standardized benchmark for skin lesion classification.
data_origin.sampling_strategy: Convenience sampling from existing clinical archive and public repository; no explicit stratification or randomization described.
data_origin.aggregation_multisource: Aggregated from two sources: hospital-centered clinical archive (majority) and ISIC public repository (minority); no description of harmonization or recoding.

population.target_population: Patients with pigmented skin lesions presenting to dermatology services.
population.inclusion_criteria: Pigmented skin lesions imaged dermoscopically and diagnosed by dermatologists.
population.missing_groups: No demographic subgroup statistics reported; underrepresentation of non-Caucasian skin types and non-Austrian populations is implied but not quantified.

annotation.annotation_method: Diagnoses assigned by dermatologists; ground truth labels derived from histopathology, expert consensus, or follow-up.
annotation.labeling_provenance: Labels derived from histopathology, expert consensus, or follow-up; some labels may reflect clinical diagnosis without histologic confirmation.
annotation.label_noise_description: Label noise exists due to inter-observer variability and reliance on clinical diagnosis where histopathology was unavailable.
